title: The load filter let "." and "1.2.3" through as 0 and 1.2, so after a high reading a malformed one started the run; the header said an unreadable load does not wait; a 0-second bound refused "after 0m"
evidence: Found in review of PR 1405 (N1, N2). tools/mac-slot.sh: a load is a well-formed number (digits, optionally a dot and digits), anything else is unreadable (unreadable first read still fails open; after a high one it keeps waiting); header states both rules; a 0-second bound prints "after 0s". Tests: tools/mac-slot.test.ts "a malformed load "."/"1.2.3" after a high one keeps waiting and refuses at the bound (lead T16)", "a malformed first load "." fails open as unreadable and starts (lead T16)", "a 0-second bound refuses saying "after 0s" (lead T16)" (failing first). US-71 AC9
